description: Vertikalt förlagda rörledningar (vertically routed pipes) are marked in a specific way on VVS-ritningar. A heavy stroke (grovt streck) placed above and/or below the dimension figure tells whether the vertical pipe penetrates the slab above, the slab below, both or neither.

entries.term_en: Heavy stroke above the dimension figure
entries.meaning_en: The vertical pipe does NOT pass through the slab above (överliggande bjälklag).

entries.term_en: Heavy stroke below the dimension figure
entries.meaning_en: The vertical pipe does NOT pass through the slab below (underliggande bjälklag).

entries.term_sv: Grovt streck både över och under dimensionsangivelsen
entries.term_en: Heavy stroke both above and below the dimension figure
entries.meaning_en: The pipe stays within the storey (ledningen stannar inom våningsplanet).
The pipe passes straight through the storey (går genom våningsplanet), i.e. through both slabs.

worked_examples.case_en: Vertical pipe passing through the storey
worked_examples.reading: Spillvatten stack, DN110, continues through both slabs.

worked_examples.plan_label: S1 over 110 with overline, plus a dash-dot branch labelled S1-110
worked_examples.reading: Pipe goes down only; no penetration of the slab above.

worked_examples.plan_label: S1 over 110 with underline, plus a branch labelled S1-110
worked_examples.reading: Pipe goes up only; no penetration of the slab below.

worked_examples.case_en: Vertical pipe contained within the storey
worked_examples.plan_label: S1 over 110 with both overline and underline
worked_examples.reading: Riser starts and ends within the same storey.

worked_examples.case_sv: Ledning i golv och på annat plan
worked_examples.case_en: Pipe in the floor and on another storey
worked_examples.reading: Stacked dimension figures list several vertical segments at the same plan position; each figure carries its own stroke notation.

worked_examples.plan_label: S1 over 110 with overline, drawn dash-dot
worked_examples.reading: Pipe belongs to the storey above; combine the line type with the stroke notation to place it.

Where several pipes share the same plan position, dimensions are stacked in reading order and each corresponds to one segment in the section. Reading a stack requires pairing each figure with its own line type and stroke.

takeoff_implication: Stroke notation plus line type is the only way to recover vertical pipe length and slab penetrations from a 2D planritning. An automated reader must detect over/underlines on dimension text and must handle stacked dimension figures at one leader point.
